newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Diphtheria outbreak closes Moscow school.
newsitem.headline: Diphtheria outbreak closes Moscow school.

text.p: At least 16 pupils of a Moscow school were taken to hospital with diphtheria and the school closed for disinfection, its director said on Friday.

Once-rare illnesses such as cholera, tuberculosis and diphtheria are making a comeback in Russia and other former Soviet republics due to a fall in healthcare standards as the countries try to adapt to a market economy.

"We have 12 children in hospital with confirmed diphtheria and another four were proved to be virus carriers. All 1,446 pupils were checked for the virus and there were no more confirmed cases," Lyudmila Kuzmina told Reuters.
The school, in Moscow's Southern district, was due to reopen on Monday, she said.

Officials at the district's administration said Moscow's chief epidemiologist and other doctors were summoned to decide on the scale of the outbreak. Diphtheria is an infectious throat disease which attacks the air passages.
